title: Advanced Filters
summary: Ignore durability or NBT, or sort by tag

blocks.text: Goal (optional): upgrade an item filter into an {item:essentialcraft5:advanced_whitelist_filter} or an {item:essentialcraft5:advanced_blacklist_filter}. It has three extra switches: ignore durability, ignore enchantments and names, or take a whole group of items by tag, such as every iron ore or wool of every color.

Prepare: a plain item filter (see [[logistics/filters]]) and 4 {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating} (see [[hoanna/void_plating]]). Put the filter in the middle and the plates above, below, left and right of it: a whitelist becomes an advanced whitelist, a blacklist an advanced blacklist.
Upgrading keeps your samples, so there is nothing to set up again.

Open the advanced filter: three buttons run down its left side; click one to toggle it. A green tick on a button means "this is compared", a red cross means "this is ignored". All three start off, so right after the upgrade it takes exactly what the plain filter took.

rows: wear does not matter: with a worn iron sword as the sample, fresh iron swords match too
only the kind of item matters: enchantments, names and contents are ignored
each sample takes a whole group of items by its chosen tag (see below)

blocks.text: Hover over a button to see whether it is on. While you hold an advanced filter, its tooltip also lists the switches that are on.

Tags are the groups the game sorts items into, such as "all iron ores" or "all logs". With <t>Match by tag</t> on, each sample slot compares by the tag chosen for it: an item in that tag counts as the same as the sample.

items: Set your samples, then click the third button to turn on <t>Match by tag</t>.

Each sample picks a "kind/material" tag by itself: an iron ingot picks <t>forge:ingots/iron</t>, iron ore picks <t>forge:ores/iron</t> (deepslate iron ore matches too, gold ore does not). A slot with a chosen tag shows a cyan <t>#</t> in its top-left corner.
To pick another tag, point at the sample slot and scroll: you cycle through all of that item's tags and "by item". The item tooltip shows the tag in use and how many items it holds.

Samples with no automatic tag, such as logs and wool, compare by item at first: scroll to <t>minecraft:logs</t> to take every log, or use a piece of wool as the sample and scroll to <t>minecraft:wool</t> to take wool of every color.
Matching by tag still compares enchantments and names unless <t>Ignore NBT</t> is on too; durability likewise follows <t>Ignore durability</t>.
Putting a different sample in a slot clears the tag chosen for that slot; with Match by tag on, the new sample picks one by itself.
Turning <t>Match by tag</t> off keeps the tags you chose; turn it back on and they are all still there.
A filter used as a sample does not match by tag; it follows its own switches.

blocks.text: A tag that is too broad lets in things you did not want: scroll to <t>forge:ingots</t> and every ingot goes through. The automatic choice is always the narrowest kind tag of the item, so check the item count in the tooltip before you change it.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: With an iron ore sample and Match by tag on, the magical hopper picks up iron ore from stone and from deepslate and leaves gold ore on the ground.

In the original mod the third switch was "Ignore Ore Dictionary" and started off, which means a fresh advanced filter compared by ore dictionary (the item groups of version 1.12). Here it is the other way round: Match by tag starts off and you turn it on yourself, so an upgrade never quietly lets in more than before. The original upgrade also wiped the samples.
Goal (optional): make a {item:essentialcraft5:void_chest}. Like the magical chest it takes up a single block, but it holds more than twice as much.
Prepare: 8 {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} (see [[hoanna/void_stone]]), laid in a ring on a crafting table with the middle left empty.

rows: can put items in and take them out from any side
the fuller it is, the stronger the signal
everything inside spills onto the ground and the chest you pick up is empty; needs a pickaxe

blocks.text: When placed, its front faces you. Right-click to open it; sneaking and right-clicking does not open it.

Its screen is a size larger than a vanilla chest's. At the largest GUI scale (including Auto) the top and bottom edges of the frame may be cut off slightly, but every slot stays visible; lower "GUI Scale" in Video Settings by one step if that bothers you.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: Opening it shows 9 rows of 13 slots.
